slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Converse: if a2 + b2 = c2 for the sides of a triangle, the triangle is right, with the right angle opposite c. If a2 + b2 > c2 (c the longest side) the triangle is acute; if a2 + b2 < c2 it is obtuse.

Proof of the converse: build a right triangle with legs a and b. Its hypotenuse is √(a2 + b2) = c, so it is congruent to the given triangle by SSS.

A Pythagoras tree grows two squares on the legs of a right triangle on top of each square. At every branch the two smaller squares' areas add to the bigger one.
